wa_fire_pit_the.blurb: The Fire Pit is a small bouldering zone right on Clayton Beach in Larrabee State Park, south of Bellingham. Eleven problems sit just a few steps along the sand from where the forest trail reaches the shore, so the walk is trivial and a crash pad is all you need. Grades span from V0 to V6, with a handful of easy and moderate lines plus a few hard ones and a long traverse. The sandstone has pockets and varied, almost gym-like holds, but it is delicate: let it dry well after rain or high tides, and expect other beach visitors around you.

wa_pandemic_boulders.blurb: Pandemic Boulders is a compact cluster of clean boulders in the trees at Lost Ledge, in Larrabee State Park near Bellingham. They were dug out in 2020 and sit uphill of the main Lost Ledge area, with the first group appearing on your left only a couple of minutes up the rock trail from the stairs. Eleven problems range from V1 to V4, mostly in the V1 to V3 band, so it suits climbers warming up or building mileage on slabs and short lines. Chuckanut sandstone here is fragile, so stay off it while wet.

wa_banded_wall.blurb: Banded Wall is one of the cliffs in the upper, north-side part of Whistler Canyon, near Oroville in the Okanogan. Its eleven routes are a genuine mix: a handful of trad lines on granite, some bolted sport routes, and two top-rope problems, with grades from 5.6 to 5.12. Most fall between 5.7 and 5.10. A dark horizontal band across the base of the main upper wall helps you pick it out from below. The crags up the canyon are remote and spread out, and reaching this one takes a longer hike than the lower walls, following cairns off the canyon trail.

wa_k_cliff.blurb: K Cliff is a south-facing wall among the Side Walls at Index, in the Skykomish Valley, with the Lower Town Wall on one side and the Inner Town Walls on the other. It has eleven routes, nearly all trad with a single bolted line, covering 5.8 to 5.11 with most in the 5.9 and 5.10 range. The face is more featured and less steep than the Lower Town Wall next door, with a blend of crack and face climbing. It is the most distant of the Side Walls from the parking lot, yet only about ten minutes on foot, and the base is flat and open.

wa_shady_lane_west.blurb: Shady Lane West is a quiet wall in the Index area of the Skykomish Valley, reached by following the Upper Wall trail for around half an hour. It has eleven routes, mostly trad with a few bolted lines, from 5.8 to 5.11 with the greatest number at 5.10. The cliff was recently cleaned and refitted with new anchor bolts. Because you can walk around to the west end and set a rope from above, it works for top-roping by groups or newer climbers.

wa_don_quixote_face.blurb: Don Quixote Face is a small granite wall at Minnehaha, Spokane's busy crag on Upriver Drive. It sits behind the Main Wall, a short stroll along a trail from the parking lot. Of its eleven routes, most are trad, with two sport lines and one top-rope. Grades start around 5.7, but the face leans hard, with a good number at 5.10 and 5.11 and a few 5.12 and 5.13 pitches. It is best known for a classic wide crack, while the bolted lines are tough and spaced out, so it is a spot for experienced climbers.
